I read your itinerary last night. It is good, but you packed it like somebody who has never flown that far.
That is fair. What would you change first?
Your carry-on. Make sure you put a charger and a plug adapter in it, because the sockets there are different.
My dad said the same thing. He also told me to double-check the hostel address before we land.
He is right. And whatever you do, don't change money at the airport. Stock up on cash at a convenience store machine instead.
Why cash? I thought everybody there paid by card.
Not in the small places. Half the restaurants we loved took nothing else, so carry some cash just to be on the safe side.
Anything about etiquette? I do not want to be the loud tourist on the train.
Then keep your voice down and never take a call in the carriage. Do bow back when somebody bows to you, and you will be fine.

Hi Mark. Last class you stood on a day that had not arrived yet and looked back at it. Today you do the next thing a trip needs, which is telling somebody else what to do. You already know the simple instruction. Take the train. Don't take a taxi. It works, but it is flat, and it gives every piece of advice exactly the same weight. English has a few ways to make an instruction heavier, and each one does a different job. Make sure, plus a full sentence, is for the one thing that must not go wrong. Make sure you keep your passport on you. And here is the first trap. After make sure, English uses the present, never will. Make sure you keep it, not make sure you will keep it. Be sure to, remember to and don't forget to all take the infinitive. Be sure to try the ramen. Don't forget to charge your phone. Whatever you do, don't, is the loudest warning the language has. Whatever you do, don't put your wallet in your back pocket. Use it once in a conversation, or it stops meaning anything. Then there is do, in front of a positive instruction, which sounds warm instead of bossy. Do try the bento at the station. And the last pattern hides a condition inside it. Leave before eight, or you will miss the fast train. Buy the pass on the first morning, and you will save money all week. Or means if you don't. And means if you do. The second trap is forget. Don't forget to buy the pass is an instruction about later. Don't forget buying it is not an instruction at all. The third trap comes from Portuguese. People say no touch, or not touch. In English a negative instruction starts with don't, or with never, and never with both. Before class, write five tips for somebody visiting Sao Paulo for the first time, with a different pattern in every one. See you in class, Mark.

Hello, and welcome in advance to Kamo River Hostel. This is Kenji, and this message goes to everybody arriving this week, so please listen to the end. First, the check-in. The front desk closes at ten at night. Whatever you do, don't arrive after ten without telling us, because the door locks and nobody will be here to open it. If your flight is late, send us a message, and we will leave a code for you. Second, the shoes. Take them off at the entrance and leave them on the shelf. The slippers are for the hallway only, so be sure to leave them outside the bathroom as well. Third, the kitchen. Do use it, because it is the best room in the house, but wash your own plates before you go to bed, or they will be in the sink with your name on them in the morning. The quiet hours start at eleven. The walls here are thin, so after eleven keep your phone calls for the garden. Now, getting around. Buy a transport card at the station on your first morning, and you will never have to think about tickets again. The buses are easy, but they are always full in the afternoon, so try to go out early. And one heads-up about money. A lot of small restaurants in Kyoto still take cash only, so make sure you have some on you before you leave in the morning. There is a machine at the convenience store on the corner. That is everything. If you have a question, the answer is probably on the board in the hall, and if it is not, ask me. See you soon.

The night before, double-check the flight time and the address of the hostel, because that is the last moment you can still fix a mistake calmly. In the morning, pack your carry-on last, with the charger, the plug adapter, your medicine and one change of clothes, so that nothing important is in the suitcase. Then leave for the airport early, or the check-in line will eat the extra hour you thought you had. On the plane, fill in the customs form before you land, and you will be out before the rest of the line. Finally, when you arrive, buy a transport card before you leave the station, and you will never have to think about tickets again.
